rules.description: Focus not moved into a non-modal overlay (popover, menu, drawer, non-modal dialog) on open
Focused element announced as "blank" or unlabelled
Focusable element announced without a role
Focus not moved into the opened dialog (review for non-modal dialogs)
Focus not returned after the dialog closed
Validation error not announced (review when inferred from an id/class)
Navigation produced no announcement (failure, 2.4.2, when the page has no title)
Emoji or icon-font glyph in the announcement
Reading order differs from visual order
Element not found with reader navigation (point to verify)
Browse mode could not be confirmed while reading
Editable field autofocused, reader starts in focus mode
Step can only be completed with a mouse
Reachable only by moving focus programmatically
Enter/Space does not activate the focused control
Composite widget items not reachable with arrows (catalogued, not emitted yet)
Focus lost after activation (catalogued, not emitted yet)
A script was needed to continue the journey
Navigation relies on keys outside the allowed set
Editable field takes focus on load (catalogued, not emitted yet)

patterns.name: Accordion (Sections With Show/Hide Functionality)
patterns.summary: An accordion is a vertically stacked set of interactive headings that each contain a title, content snippet, or thumbnail representing a section of content.

patterns.name: Alert
patterns.summary: An alert is an element that displays a brief, important message in a way that attracts the user's attention without interrupting the user's task.

patterns.name: Alert and Message Dialogs
patterns.summary: An alert dialog is a modal dialog that interrupts the user's workflow to communicate an important message and acquire a response.

patterns.name: Breadcrumb
patterns.summary: A breadcrumb trail consists of a list of links to the parent pages of the current page in hierarchical order.

patterns.name: Button
patterns.summary: A button is a widget that enables users to trigger an action or event, such as submitting a form, opening a dialog, canceling an action, or performing a delete operation.

patterns.name: Carousel (Slide Show or Image Rotator)
patterns.summary: A carousel presents a set of items, referred to as slides, by sequentially displaying a subset of one or more slides.

patterns.name: Checkbox
patterns.summary: WAI-ARIA supports two types of checkbox widgets: dual-state checkboxes toggle between two choices -- checked and not checked -- and tri-state checkboxes, which allow an additional third state known as partially checked.

patterns.name: Combobox
patterns.summary: A combobox is an input widget that has an associated popup.

patterns.name: Dialog (Modal)
patterns.summary: A dialog is a window overlaid on either the primary window or another dialog window.

patterns.name: Disclosure (Show/Hide)
patterns.summary: A disclosure is a widget that enables content to be either collapsed (hidden) or expanded (visible).

patterns.name: Feed
patterns.summary: A feed is a section of a page that automatically loads new sections of content as the user scrolls.

patterns.name: Grid (Interactive Tabular Data and Layout Containers)
patterns.summary: A grid widget is a container that enables users to navigate the information or interactive elements it contains using directional navigation keys, such as arrow keys, Home, and End.

patterns.name: Landmarks
patterns.summary: Landmarks are a set of eight roles that identify the major sections of a page.

patterns.name: Link
patterns.summary: A link widget provides an interactive reference to a resource.

patterns.name: Listbox
patterns.summary: A listbox widget presents a list of options and allows a user to select one or more of them.

patterns.name: Menu and Menubar
patterns.summary: A menu is a widget that offers a list of choices to the user, such as a set of actions or functions.

patterns.name: Menu Button
patterns.summary: A menu button is a button that opens a menu as described in the Menu and Menubar Pattern.

patterns.name: Meter
patterns.summary: A meter is a graphical display of a numeric value that varies within a defined range.

patterns.name: Radio Group
patterns.summary: A radio group is a set of checkable buttons, known as radio buttons, where no more than one of the buttons can be checked at a time.

patterns.name: Slider
patterns.summary: A slider is an input where the user selects a value from within a given range.

patterns.name: Slider (Multi-Thumb)
patterns.summary: A multi-thumb slider implements the Slider Pattern but includes two or more thumbs, often on a single rail.

patterns.name: Spinbutton
patterns.summary: A spinbutton is an input widget that restricts its value to a set or range of discrete values.

patterns.name: Switch
patterns.summary: A switch is an input widget that allows users to choose one of two values: on or off.

patterns.name: Table
patterns.summary: Like an HTML table element, a WAI-ARIA table is a static tabular structure containing one or more rows that each contain one or more cells; it is not an interactive widget.

patterns.name: Tabs
patterns.summary: Tabs are a set of layered sections of content, known as tab panels, that display one panel of content at a time.

patterns.name: Toolbar
patterns.summary: A toolbar is a container for grouping a set of controls, such as buttons, menubuttons, or checkboxes.

patterns.name: Tooltip
patterns.summary: A tooltip is a popup that displays information related to an element when the element receives keyboard focus or the mouse hovers over it.

patterns.name: Tree View
patterns.summary: A tree view widget presents a hierarchical list.

patterns.name: Treegrid
patterns.summary: A treegrid widget presents a hierarchical data grid consisting of tabular information that is editable or interactive.

patterns.name: Window Splitter
patterns.summary: A window splitter is a moveable separator between two sections, or panes, of a window that enables users to change the relative size of the panes.
